audit.originality: All seven prompts, all values and both figure briefs are original. The 42 complete mapped official P2 questions and 50 mapped leaves supplied assessment patterns only.
audit.scope: Restricted to deriving and using classical translational kinetic energy, signed kinetic-energy changes, ratios and supplied mechanical-energy ledgers. Momentum, collision classification, springs, electric fields and nuclear contexts from mixed evidence are not required.
audit.evidence: The available checkout has no controlled Topic 5 lesson map or lesson-knowledge map. The 9702_t05_cm03_l05 handoff controls prior kinetic-energy knowledge, while the frozen title and official use outcome 9702_t05_m02_o04 define new scope. All P2 enrichment leaves mapped to the derivation and use outcomes were traced to their complete canonical question and official mark scheme.
audit.learner_answer_separation: questions.json contains only prompts, options, response schemas and planned figure metadata. Answers, feedback, criteria, hints and walkthroughs are answer-side.

evidence.role: Retrieve the formula derived in Lesson 5 and use it in one direct calculation.

hints: Recall the mass-speed relationship derived in Lesson 5.
Square 4.0 m s^-1 before multiplying by the mass and one-half.

walkthrough.text: State the Lesson 5 result E_K = 1/2 mv^2.
Substitute m = 2.5 kg and v = 4.0 m s^-1.
The cart's kinetic energy is 20 J.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes 2.5 kg and 4.0 m s^-1 to obtain 20 J

hints: Identify the physical feature of an object that gives it this energy.

walkthrough.text: Kinetic energy belongs to an object when it is moving.
Use the controlled wording: energy that an object has because of its motion.

ai_rubric.observable: Defines kinetic energy as energy that an object has because of its motion

evidence.role: Diagnose the squared speed dependence without a full numerical calculation.

hints: Hold mass fixed and track what happens to the squared speed factor.

walkthrough.text: Use E_K = 1/2 mv^2.
The mass and one-half factors are unchanged, so only v^2 changes.
Replacing v by 3v multiplies v^2 by 3^2 = 9.
Therefore option D is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects D because tripling speed multiplies kinetic energy by nine

evidence.role: Compare two kinetic energies while both mass and speed differ.

hints: Write one proportional expression for each cart and cancel the common one-half factor.

walkthrough.text: For P, E_K,P = 1/2(2m)v^2.
The ratio is [m(4v^2)]/[2mv^2] = 2.
Therefore option C is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C from the kinetic-energy ratio [m(2v)^2]/[(2m)v^2] = 2

evidence.role: Distinguish final-minus-initial change from the positive magnitude of a loss.

hints: Write change as final value minus initial value before placing either speed into the formula.

walkthrough.text: Use Delta E_K = E_K,final - E_K,initial.
The final speed is 3.0 m s^-1 and the initial speed is 7.0 m s^-1.
The negative result represents an 80 J decrease, so option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B because kinetic-energy change is final minus initial, 1/2 x 4.0 x (3.0^2 - 7.0^2)

evidence.role: Move from a signed two-speed calculation to rearranging the same formula for speed.
Calculate a positive final-minus-initial kinetic-energy change.

hints: Use one mass with the final squared speed minus the initial squared speed.
Keep the answer in joules until the last conversion.

walkthrough.text: Use Delta E_K = 1/2 m(v^2 - u^2).
Substitute m = 620 kg, v = 11 m s^-1 and u = 4.0 m s^-1.
This is 32.55 kJ, or 32.6 kJ to three significant figures. The positive sign agrees with the increase in speed.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses kinetic-energy change as 1/2 m(v^2 - u^2)
Substitutes 620 kg, 11 m s^-1 and 4.0 m s^-1 with final speed first
Obtains an increase of 32 550 J or 32.6 kJ

evidence.role: Rearrange kinetic energy for speed after an energy-unit conversion.

hints: Convert the kilojoule value before isolating the squared speed.
Take the positive square root only after dividing by the mass.

walkthrough.text: Convert 55.8 kJ to 55 800 J.
Rearrange E_K = 1/2 mv^2 to v = sqrt(2E_K/m).
The speed is 13.416 m s^-1, which is 13.4 m s^-1 to three significant figures.

ai_rubric.observable: Converts 55.8 kJ to 55 800 J and uses v = sqrt(2E_K/m)

evidence.role: Combine initial kinetic energy, gravitational transfer, dissipative loss and final-speed recovery in one original chain.
Establish non-zero initial kinetic energy for the later ledger.

hints: Use the speed at the top, not the unknown bottom speed.

walkthrough.text: At the top, m = 1.8 kg and v = 3.0 m s^-1.
E_K,top = 8.1 J.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses E_K = 1/2 mv^2 with the top speed

evidence.role: Recover the gravitational input needed by the energy ledger.

hints: Use the vertical height change, not the distance along the ramp.

walkthrough.text: Use the magnitude of the decrease, mg Delta h.
Substitute 1.8 kg, 9.81 m s^-2 and 2.4 m.
The decrease is 1.8 x 9.81 x 2.4 = 42.3792 J, or 42.4 J.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the magnitude of the gravitational potential-energy decrease as mg Delta h
Obtains a gravitational potential-energy decrease of 42.4 J

evidence.role: Account for a non-zero initial store and a dissipative transfer before finding final kinetic energy.

hints: Start with the top kinetic energy, add the energy released by descending, then remove the stated thermal transfer.

walkthrough.text: The pod begins with 8.1 J of kinetic energy.
The descent releases 42.3792 J from gravitational potential energy.
Resistance transfers 9.5 J to thermal energy.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms the ledger E_K,bottom = E_K,top + gravitational potential-energy decrease - 9.5 J

evidence.role: Recover speed from the carried final energy and close the ledger numerically.

hints: Use the carried bottom kinetic energy in the rearranged kinetic-energy formula.
For the check, compare total energy available with final kinetic plus thermal transfer.

walkthrough.text: Use v = sqrt(2E_K,bottom/m).
The speed is 6.75 m s^-1 to three significant figures.
Check the whole ledger: input available is 8.1 + 42.3792 = 50.4792 J; output is 40.9792 + 9.5 = 50.4792 J.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the bottom kinetic energy to obtain speed 6.75 m s^-1
Checks numerically that 8.1 J + 42.4 J equals 41.0 J + 9.5 J within rounding
